official_measurement_examples.name: 42-day response period
official_measurement_examples.fact: After acknowledging a removal notice the LPA has 42 days to issue permission or a retention notice; silence after the period can permit the notified removal subject to the regulations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Two-year removal window
official_measurement_examples.fact: National guidance states a written permission to remove a hedgerow can be acted on for up to 2 years from the date of the written notice.

official_measurement_examples.name: Important hedgerow criteria
official_measurement_examples.fact: Important status depends on statutory archaeological historical ecological and landscape criteria rather than simple map presence alone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Garden hedge exclusion
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Hedgerows Regulations generally do not apply to ordinary domestic garden hedges; scope depends on land use and statutory criteria.

official_measurement_examples.name: Removal versus trimming
official_measurement_examples.fact: Removal controls under the 1997 Regulations are distinct from agricultural cutting and trimming management rules updated 31 March 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Retention notice distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A hedgerow retention notice controls removal but does not grant or refuse planning permission for development on the parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Wildlife law separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Compliance with hedgerow removal rules does not remove duties under wildlife law such as protection of nesting birds or protected species.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Hedgerow status does not establish title exact legal boundary buildable area or final development yield.

core_rules: removal notice is not planning permission
retention notice is not title evidence
two-year window is not perpetual permission
garden hedges can fall outside scope
removal and trimming regimes remain distinct
cutting derogation does not authorise removal
hedgerow permission does not replace wildlife law
wildlife compliance does not prove hedgerow permission
hedgerow map is not cadastral boundary
hedgerow status does not calculate yield
absence from one dataset is not definitive absence
no parcel hedgerow clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
